C05-M03-L01-F1.title: Host discovery probe families and what they prove
C05-M03-L01-F1.caption: Each probe family proves a host is live in a different way and fails in a different way.
C05-M03-L01-F1.alt: Table with six rows. ARP request, Nmap -PR, proven by an ARP reply, works only on the local segment. ICMP echo, -PE, proven by an echo reply, often dropped at perimeters. ICMP timestamp, -PP, proven by a timestamp reply, sometimes answered when echo is blocked. TCP SYN probe, -PS with ports, proven by SYN/ACK or RST, needs a port the filter allows. TCP ACK probe, -PA with ports, proven by RST, stateful firewalls drop it. UDP probe, -PU with ports, proven by ICMP port unreachable, open UDP ports are often silent.
rows: Needs a port the filter allows
C05-M03-L01-F1.note: A host is marked up when any probe gets a reply; 'down' only means every probe used went unanswered.

C05-M03-L01-F2.title: From signed scope to verified live-host list
C05-M03-L01-F2.caption: The safe discovery procedure: verify the target list without touching targets, then probe.
C05-M03-L01-F2.alt: Top-to-bottom flow of six steps: signed scope (scope.md); target file (targets.txt plus exclude.txt); list scan with -sL -n, which sends no packets to targets; review and exclude, checking the address count against the scope; discovery with -sn --reason, the only active step; live-host list saved with -oA and timestamped. A loop arrow returns from the last step to review when results are unexpected.

steps.label: List scan (-sL -n)
steps.sub: expands targets, no packets to them

loop.label: unexpected result: return to review before probing again

C05-M03-L01-F2.note: Only one of the six steps sends packets to targets; the others prevent it reaching the wrong ones.
